question: If HOF Village sells the Village Media Company to an outside buyer, can the Hall of Fame (PFHOF) end the agreement?
expected_answer: Yes. If the Village Media Company stops being controlled by (or under common control with) HOFV, including through a merger, that is a Change of Control and PFHOF may terminate immediately on notice (§4.4). Separately, the Village Media Company cannot assign or transfer the agreement without PFHOF's written consent (§7.5).
source_span: if a Change of Control occurs at any time during the Term, PFHOF shall have the right to terminate this Agreement immediately upon giving notice
source_note: §4.4 (§7.5 is a separate assignment point): "if a Change of Control occurs at any time during the Term, PFHOF shall have the right to terminate this Agreement immediately upon giving notice"
pass_rule: Judge: must say Yes, cite §4.4, mention immediate termination on notice
critique: Correct: Yes; a sale that ends HOFV's control is a Change of Control, so PFHOF can terminate immediately on notice (§4.4). Wrong if it requires cause or a cure period, or relies only on the assignment clause (§7.5) without citing §4.4.

question: After the agreement ends, can the Village Media Company keep distributing shows it made using Hall of Fame content?
expected_answer: Yes, for limited time. It may keep exploiting the HOFV Works it created for the length of the license term PFHOF granted for each work under §2.3, which must be at least five years (§2.1). PFHOF still owns the underlying PFHOF Works (§2.5).
source_span: after the termination or expiration of this Agreement, the Village Media Company and its permitted licensees shall continue to have the right to fully exploit, use, and Exploit the HOFV Works for the length of the term of the license granted by PFHOF
source_note: §2.1 (supported by §2.3 and §2.5): "after the termination or expiration of this Agreement, the Village Media Company and its permitted licensees shall continue to have the right to fully exploit, use, and Exploit the HOFV Works for the length of the term of the license granted by PFHOF"
pass_rule: Judge: must say Yes, limited to each work's license term, minimum 5 years
critique: Correct: Yes, but time-limited; each HOFV Work can be exploited for its §2.3 license term, at least five years (§2.1). Wrong if it says the rights last forever, end at termination, or that Village Media owns the underlying Hall of Fame content.

question: Can Ingram Micro exit after year one without paying a termination penalty?
expected_answer: Yes. Either party can terminate at any time without cause on 90 days' written notice (§15.B), so Ingram does not even need to wait for year one to end. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, neither party owes the other any amounts, costs or damages because of expiration or early termination (§15.C, §15.D).
source_span: no party is liable to the other for any dollar amounts, costs or damages by reason of the expiration or earlier termination of the Agreement
source_note: §15.D (see also §15.B, §15.C): "no party is liable to the other for any dollar amounts, costs or damages by reason of the expiration or earlier termination of the Agreement"
pass_rule: Judge: must say Yes, 90 days' notice, and no termination payment
critique: Correct: Yes; either party can terminate at any time without cause on 90 days' written notice (§15.B), with no termination payment (§15.C, §15.D). Wrong if it says Ingram must wait for the renewal date, owes a penalty, or states a notice period other than 90 days.

question: If a NETGEAR product failure causes Ingram Micro to lose customer data, can Ingram recover those losses from NETGEAR?
expected_answer: No. §16 excludes, for both parties, damages resulting from inaccurate or lost data, loss of use or profits, and consequential or indirect damages, even if the party was warned. Other damages are subject to an overall cap whose amount is redacted [*]; the only carve-outs are infringement claims (§14.A) and the bodily-injury/property-damage indemnity (§16.A).
source_span: IN NO EVENT WILL EITHER PARTY OR THEIR RESPECTIVE PARENT CORPORATIONS OR SUPPLIERS BE LIABLE FOR (1) THE COST OF SUBSTITUTE PROCUREMENT, SPECIAL, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, OR (2) ANY DAMAGES RESULTING FROM INACCURATE OR LOST DATA
source_note: §16 (Limitation of Liability): "IN NO EVENT WILL EITHER PARTY OR THEIR RESPECTIVE PARENT CORPORATIONS OR SUPPLIERS BE LIABLE FOR (1) THE COST OF SUBSTITUTE PROCUREMENT, SPECIAL, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, OR (2) ANY DAMAGES RESULTING FROM INACCURATE OR LOST DATA"
pass_rule: Judge: must say No and cite the lost-data exclusion; FAIL if a cap amount is invented
critique: Correct: No; §16 excludes lost-data, lost-profit and consequential damages for both parties. Wrong if it says the loss is recoverable up to the cap, states a cap amount (it is redacted), or treats the §16.A indemnity as covering data loss.

Ingram could still terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice (§15.B).

question: Can Marathon Petroleum (the Shipper) back out before the pipeline starts service, and what would it cost?
expected_answer: Yes, if MPL is in compliance. The Shipper must notify MPL within 180 days of the Project's in-service date so MPL can offer the capacity to others. If it misses that window, or MPL cannot fully replace its committed volumes, the Shipper reimburses its pro rata share of actual and committed Construction Costs plus a 10% administrative fee. This is treated as liquidated damages and is MPL's sole and exclusive remedy.
source_span: Shipper will reimburse MPL for Shipper's pro rata portion of actual and committed Construction Costs, plus, an administrative fee of ten (10) percent of said costs
source_note: §10.5 (cross-references §3.8, whose text is about Prepaid Transportation Credits and has no Unsubscribed Capacity process): "Shipper will reimburse MPL for Shipper's pro rata portion of actual and committed Construction Costs, plus, an administrative fee of ten (10) percent of said costs"
pass_rule: Judge: must mention 180-day notice, pro rata construction costs + 10% fee, liquidated damages
critique: Correct: Yes, with notice within 180 days of the in-service date; if late or volumes aren't replaced, Shipper pays pro rata construction costs plus a 10% fee as liquidated damages, MPL's sole remedy (§10.5). Wrong if it says Shipper can exit freely, owes the full contract value or deficiency payments for the whole term, or omits the 10% fee.

question: What happens if the Shipper ships less than its committed volume in a quarter? Is that money lost?
expected_answer: It pays a Quarterly Deficiency Payment: (Quarterly Volume Commitment minus actual deliveries) × the applicable Tariff Rate (§3.5). The payment is not lost straight away: it becomes Prepaid Transportation Credits usable against shipments above the commitment in the next four quarters, after which unused credits expire (§3.6).
source_span: The dollar amount of any Quarterly Deficiency Payment paid by Shipper shall constitute prepayment for transportation of Product by Shipper on the Pipeline
source_note: §3.5; §3.6: "The dollar amount of any Quarterly Deficiency Payment paid by Shipper shall constitute prepayment for transportation of Product by Shipper on the Pipeline"
pass_rule: Judge: must describe the deficiency payment AND the four-quarter credit
critique: Correct: Shipper pays shortfall × tariff rate (§3.5), which becomes a credit usable against over-commitment shipments in the next four quarters, then expires (§3.6). Wrong if it says the payment is simply forfeited, refundable, or usable indefinitely.

pass_rule: Judge: must say no exclusivity; FAIL if it claims an exclusivity obligation

question: If Integra misses a minimum payment, can PcoMed terminate the agreement or sue for the shortfall?
expected_answer: No. PcoMed's sole and exclusive remedy is to convert Integra's exclusive rights to non-exclusive, and Integra has no liability for failing to pay the Minimum Payment (§2.4). Conversion requires written notice and a 45-day cure period (§3.2), after which the non-exclusive fee rates apply (§2.2; rates redacted).
source_span: PcoMed's conversion right is PcoMed's sole and exclusive remedy for Integra's failure to satisfy the Minimum Payment
source_note: §2.4; §3.2: "PcoMed's conversion right is PcoMed's sole and exclusive remedy for Integra's failure to satisfy the Minimum Payment"
pass_rule: Judge: must say No, conversion to non-exclusive is the sole remedy, 45-day cure
critique: Correct: No; PcoMed's sole remedy is converting Integra's rights to non-exclusive after notice and a 45-day cure (§2.4, §3.2), and Integra has no liability for the shortfall. Wrong if it says PcoMed can terminate for material breach (§4.3) or sue for the unpaid minimum.

question: Who owns an invention that the parties develop jointly during the term?
expected_answer: It depends on what it relates to. PcoMed owns it if it relates primarily to PcoMed Technology; Integra owns it if it relates primarily to Integra Products. The parties may agree that a joint invention is owned by both. Each party's existing technology stays with it.
source_span: shall be the property of (i) PcoMed if it relates primarily to the PcoMed Technology and (ii) Integra if it relates primarily to the Integra Products
source_note: §8.1: "shall be the property of (i) PcoMed if it relates primarily to the PcoMed Technology and (ii) Integra if it relates primarily to the Integra Products"
pass_rule: Judge: must give the "relates primarily to" test for both parties
critique: Correct: It depends; PcoMed owns it if it relates primarily to PcoMed Technology, Integra if primarily to Integra Products, and joint ownership only if agreed (§8.1). Wrong if it says joint inventions are automatically owned 50/50 or always by one party.

pass_rule: Judge: must say no termination for convenience; FAIL if it describes one
acceptable_alternative: No convenience right exists; termination is for cause only (§4.3). A found:true answer saying this is acceptable.

expected_answer: Only for serious and justified reasons or by mutual consent, with at least 30 days' written notice by certified letter or PEC. Withdrawal only affects the future. Kiromic must cover Molipharma's expenses incurred and committed on the research programs up to receipt of the notice.

expected_answer: IP on the Results is owned jointly, 50/50, unless the parties agree in writing to adjust shares by contribution (§6). For SARS-CoV-2, economic rights in Europe belong exclusively to Molipharma and in the US exclusively to Kiromic; the rest of the world is split at redacted percentages (§7).

pass_rule: Judge: must state 50/50 joint ownership AND Europe = Molipharma, US = Kiromic
critique: Correct: Results IP is owned 50/50 unless agreed otherwise (§6); SARS-CoV-2 economic rights go to Molipharma in Europe and Kiromic in the US, with the rest of the world split at redacted percentages (§7). Wrong if it gives all IP to one party, swaps Europe and US, or states rest-of-world percentages.
